features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: The level of formal academic training in computer science or a related technical field the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Whether the letter shows concrete design ownership of agent-based systems and their control boundaries, orchestration, or supervision.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or autonomous-tooling experience is mentioned.
Agents or automation are mentioned vaguely, with little architectural detail.
The letter shows clear experience building agent-based workflows or pipelines.
The letter gives a detailed agentic architecture, such as bounded actions, contracts, logging, auditing, permissions, or a clear Go and Python division of responsibility.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI maturity
features.description: The depth of real production AI or LLM experience the letter shows, especially around reliability, evaluation, and safe deployment.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Claim substantiation
features.description: How concretely the letter supports its claims with owned examples, mechanisms, results, and observable effects.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists qualities or interests with little supporting evidence.
Includes a few examples but limited detail on ownership or effect.
Gives concrete examples of work with enough detail to make the claims credible.
Repeatedly ties claims to specific actions and clear outcomes or impact.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the letter frames security tooling as helping developers through safer defaults, lower friction, and empathy for internal users.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: Emphasis on reliability, maintainability, correctness, and long-term operational care in security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central and production-grade Go appears in the applicant's recent engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: How well the letter forms a structured, connected career story rather than a loose list of claims.

levels.descriptor: Reads as a disconnected inventory of facts or a compliance-style form letter.
Has some stated motivation, but the link from prior work to this role is thin or mechanical.
Presents a coherent progression from prior experience to the target role.
Tells a memorable, well-shaped story that makes the move into this role feel natural, intentional, and earned.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: How memorable, individualized, and non-template-like the letter's voice or framing is.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Evidence of ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary product engineering, such as CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for public code through contribution, maintenance, or upstream fixes that serve external users or dependencies.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition and seriousness of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation for foundational infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production engineering experience
features.description: The amount and breadth of hands-on experience the letter conveys in shipping, maintaining, testing, and operating production software.

levels.descriptor: Meets the minimum bar only, with limited production history or few concrete examples of launched services.
Shows a solid early-career production record, with some launch and maintenance experience but modest cumulative depth.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with repeated launch and maintenance ownership across multiple production services.
Shows extensive production depth, combining long tenure with repeated delivery and operation of many production services.

features.name: Programming language breadth
features.description: The range of programming languages the letter presents beyond the core language requirements.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How deep and production-relevant the applicant's Python experience appears for services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Mentions Python briefly or only as light scripting.
Describes regular Python use for tooling, automation, or services.
Shows deep Python ownership across production services or critical internal tooling.

features.name: Requirement mapping
features.description: How explicitly the letter maps the applicant's background to the job posting's stated qualifications, responsibilities, or requirements.

levels.descriptor: Makes little direct connection to the posting beyond naming the role.
Mentions some relevant qualifications, but the mapping to the posting is mostly implicit.
Clearly addresses several core requirements or responsibilities from the posting.
Systematically maps experience to the posting, with explicit coverage of the main requirements and responsibilities.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: How specifically the letter explains why this exact role is an appealing and logical next step for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses through reviews, threat modeling, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation mission understanding
features.description: How well the letter shows understanding of the team's specific mission of scaling security work through automation, triage, agents, or platform systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows little understanding of the specific security problem this team solves.
The letter shows general interest in security engineering, but mostly at a broad level.
The letter clearly articulates goals like reducing manual security work or making the secure path easier for developers.
The letter shows nuanced insight into bottlenecks such as scarce expert attention, vulnerability triage, lifecycle embedding, bounded agents, or similar operational realities.

features.name: Security collaboration mindset
features.description: Whether the applicant emphasizes learning from and collaborating with security specialists and other internal users rather than working in isolation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The rigor of formal third-party security certifications or other explicit external validation presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Whether the letter articulates a clear point of view about what security engineering is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinct point of view beyond wanting the job.
Uses generic statements about liking security or impact.
States a clear principle or worldview about security engineering.
Uses a memorable principle that frames the letter and signals mature judgment.

features.name: Vulnerability automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: How free the letter is from distracting spelling, typographical, grammatical, or surface-level writing errors.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly recur as the same construct as a broader criterion.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.
